title: Apply online for a building information certificate
summary: You can apply online for a building information certificate (BIC) if you suspect work was done on a property without proper council or private certifier approvals.
intro:
If you’re buying or selling a property and you suspect work may have been done without appropriate council or private certifier approvals, you can apply for a building information certificate (BIC).

This certificate ensures the whole or part of the building covered by the certificate won’t be subject to any regulatory action by the local council for 7 years.

Regulatory action could include:

You can apply online for a BIC via the NSW Planning Portal.

Before you apply, check with your local council to ensure it is accepting online applications through the NSW Planning Portal.
who_can_apply: Another person, with the consent of the property owner
The purchaser of a property under a contract of sale (including the purchaser’s solicitor or agent)
A public authority that has notified the owner of its intention to apply for the certificate
what_you_need: An original, or certified copy, of a survey report and plan (if the land is zoned as residential), or a survey report (if the land is situated in other zones)
Specific documents requested by council such as building plans, specifications, or certificates (if applicable)
Copies of documents for uploading (the survey report and plan must represent the property and buildings as existing at the time of submitting the application)
Payment for the service (fees are listed on the NSW Planning Portal Service website)

how_to_steps.text: You'll have the option to log in using your MyServiceNSW Account.
Follow the prompts to complete your application.

contact: Submit an online enquiry or contact Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure.

faqs.q: What does a building information certificate do?
faqs.a: This certificate ensures that the whole or part of the building covered by the certificate will not be subject to any regulatory action by the local council for 7 years.

faqs.q: Who can apply for a building information certificate?
faqs.a: The owner of the property, another person (with the owner's consent), the purchaser of a property under a contract of sale, or a public authority that has notified the owner of its intention to apply.

faqs.q: Where can I apply for a BIC?
faqs.a: You can apply online for a BIC via the NSW Planning Portal. Before applying, check with your local council to ensure they accept online applications through the NSW Planning Portal.
